implement.instructions: After npm run check passes, if your change can alter what the carnival shows, capture it. Run node scripts/screenshot.mjs .screenshots, which saves the midway and every game. When those default views don't show your change clearly, first write a plan file outside the repository and pass it as a second argument: the top of the script describes how to crop to an area, press keys, hold keys to walk and click. Look at the pictures, and fix the plan if they miss your change. When your change involves movement, animation or playing a game, add a picture with "video": true to the plan, which saves <name>.webm and <name>.gif. GitHub won't play a .webm in a pull request, so show the GIF as ![name](<raw link to the .gif>) and put a [Full video](<raw link to the .webm>) link under it. Keep videos short, under about 10 seconds, because they stay in the repository's history. Exit code 2 means every capture finished but a page logged an error, and 3 means a capture also failed: for either, list those errors in the pull request, and fix them if your change caused them. Only embed files that exist. If a GIF is missing, link its .webm instead. Commit only the .screenshots folder and push, and note the commit with git rev-parse HEAD. Then run git rm -r .screenshots, commit and push, so the final diff has no screenshots. In the pull request body, under a ## Screenshots heading, show each picture that's useful as ![name](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/<that commit>/.screenshots/<name>.png). Skip all of this when nothing visible changed. If the script exits 1 or 3, say which captures failed in one sentence in the pull request and carry on: a screenshot problem never holds up the change.
